reading.body:
Upstage's Solar family is API-only and closed-weight, so its three models can be rented but never self-hosted.

The family spans three releases in eight months, from Solar Pro 3 in January 2026 to Solar Mini 4 in September 2026. Every version supports reasoning and text-only input and output. Context windows run from 131,072 to 524,288 tokens, and maximum output from 117,964 to 131,072 tokens. That combination suits long documents and long generated answers rather than short chat turns.

Pricing falls as the family moves forward. Solar Pro 3 costs $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.6 per million output tokens. Solar Pro 4 costs $0.09 and $0.36. Solar Mini 4 costs $0.05 and $0.2. The newest and cheapest model also has the largest context window, so capability and price are not trading against each other here. For AI builders, this is a family priced for volume, where cost scales with tokens consumed rather than with access.

The data covers only the OpenRouter catalog: three models, their prices, context limits, and release dates. It does not include benchmarks, parameter counts, training compute, or any measure of quality, so nothing here says how these models perform against alternatives. It also says nothing about the data centers or power behind them, and nothing about where Upstage trains or serves them.

paragraphs: Upstage Solar is the model family from the developer Upstage. The catalog page describes Solar LLM for advanced language processing, alongside specialized models for document parsing, and lists Solar Pro 4, Solar Mini 4, Solar Open 2, Solar Pro 3, Solar Pro 2, Solar Pro, and Solar Decide. Upstage says Solar Pro 4 is its flagship model, specialized for agentic use, and particularly strong at document-based work, coding, and business-related tasks. Upstage says Solar Mini 4 is its cost-efficient, compact model for agentic use cases where response speed and cost matter, with 35B total parameters and 3B active. Solar Open 2 is described as an open-weight model optimized for agentic use, with 250B total and 15B active parameters in an MoE architecture, a context window of up to 1M tokens, and official support for Korean, English, and Japanese. Solar Pro 3 is described as a Mixture-of-Experts language model with 102B total parameters and 12B active parameters per forward pass.

The family is organized into versions and aliases. The changelog states that Solar Pro 3, the solar-pro3 alias and all of its versions, will be fully deprecated on October 30, 2026 (KST), and that requests naming it will return an error after that date. Solar Pro 4 is named solar-pro4, and Solar Mini 4 is named solar-mini4. Solar Decide is available in beta on the POST /v1/systemone endpoint, served on Solar Mini 4, with a 512K context length. Upstage offers the models through the Upstage Console and the Upstage API, and the catalog page states that all models listed can also be deployed on a virtual private cloud (VPC) with any cloud provider or on-premises, unless otherwise noted. Solar Open 2 is available as open weights on Hugging Face.

price_limits.summary: Across the 3 versions, input prices run from $0.05 to $0.15 per million tokens and output prices from $0.2 to $0.6. Solar Mini 4 is the cheapest, at $0.05 per million input tokens and $0.2 per million output tokens. Solar Mini 4 has the largest context window, 524,288 tokens.

family_reading.text: Upstage Solar is an API only, text in and text out family. All three catalog versions support reasoning, and none publish open weights, so you cannot self host. Context windows run from 131072 to 524288 tokens, with maximum output from 117964 to 131072 tokens, which suits long documents and long generated answers. Pricing is low per million tokens, from $0.05 input and $0.2 output on Solar Mini 4 up to $0.15 input and $0.6 output on Solar Pro 3, so cost scales with volume rather than access. The facts suggest the family fits high volume text and reasoning work over large inputs, where API use is acceptable. Limits are the text only modalities, no open weights, and the higher per token cost of the older Pro 3 tier.
